notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Some Tennessee cities run their own school systems; where this one does, school spending is included and left out of the services and overhead shares. Residents also pay Monroe County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($754,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Tennessee city candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-17. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Tennessee yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Sweetwater Police Department operates eight Flock Safety automated license plate readers as of September 2025.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS016756, citing Public Records From the EFF via Pittsboro Police - See note

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Sweetwater Police Department has access to SoundThinking's CrimeTracer (formerly Coplink X) investigative platform through a statewide contract announced in April 2021.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012670, citing PR News Wire

redFlags.unscoredReason: Not scored: every police department in the state has this through a statewide contract, so it is not a local decision.
